variants.name: 02 — Courtyard Production and Sale
variants.prompt:
EDIT the attached OpenCompany cat workplace banner to correct its visual storytelling. The previous image shows unattended trays labeled TOKENS, WORK and REVENUE while employees sit behind them. The new image must show the employees PHYSICALLY CONVERTING TOKENS INTO FINISHED WORK and a separate CUSTOMER RECEIVING THE WORK AND PAYING FOR IT. This is the highest-priority change.

REMOVE AND REPLACE
Remove the entire row of three foreground display trays and the passive piles of tokens, finished cards and money. Do not reproduce that decorative three-tray arrangement. Remove the large generic revenue coin pile. Replace it with a connected active workbench and an actual two-way customer transaction. Every main story object must be held by a character, entering an employee's active tool, emerging as a deliverable, or being exchanged between two characters.

RETAIN THE APPROVED DESIGN FAMILY
A recognizable silver laptop contains a beautiful miniature professional company: warm crafted wood, cream plaster, professional cat clothing, sophisticated mature feline character design, subtle fur detail and clear editorial typography. Keep the original grumpy brown Persian boss, the six existing role-specific cats, the brand and the overall warm artistic quality. The architecture and staff positions MAY change substantially to make actions clear. The prior rigid two-row role placement is NOT mandatory for this composition.

EXACTLY SIX EMPLOYEES, ONE BOSS, ONE CUSTOMER — EIGHT CHARACTERS
- Builder: ginger tabby, slate-blue rolled-cuff overshirt; focused software maker.
- Grower: white coat with a charcoal ear patch, sage blazer and terracotta shirt; expressive content/campaign maker.
- Chief of Staff: black-and-white tuxedo, navy waistcoat, cream collar; composed organizer.
- Front Desk: cream colorpoint with sable ears, burgundy jacket and headset; welcoming service professional.
- Researcher: calico, oatmeal cardigan and round spectacles; curious and analytical.
- Treasurer: silver tabby, forest-green waistcoat; precise payment operator.
- Boss: stocky chocolate-brown Persian with a cream muzzle, lowered brows, narrowed eyes and grumpy frown; charcoal suit and gold tie. He actively points at the employees' work in progress. A small dollar-shaped lapel pin or dollar-marked ledger keeps his money-minded personality visible, but he is NOT the paying customer.
- Customer: a separate solid blue-gray shorthair cat wearing a bright teal coat with a small mustard shoulder bag, friendly interested expression, no employee headset or tools. The customer is visiting from OUTSIDE the laptop workplace and is the source of the payment. Distinct from the silver-striped Treasurer, the tuxedo coordinator and the boss.

SHOW THE CAUSAL ACTIONS CLEARLY
1. TOKEN INPUT: At the far-left end of the employee workbench, the Researcher's paw visibly holds a large cyan token tile HALFWAY INSERTED into a cyan-edged input dock attached directly to an active browser/AI workstation. The input dock has a large clear "TOKENS" label. Show just two spare cyan tiles nearby, not a huge unattended pile. The tile and paw must touch the input slot; it cannot simply float nearby.
2. ACTIVE PRODUCTION: The ginger Builder works at a code screen and pulls an ivory software deliverable card from a slot on that same workstation. Beside this, the Grower creates a visual campaign page from their editing screen. A short transparent or open physical channel links the token-input dock to these active tools. Show the transition from cyan input marks to structured code, charts and document graphics inside the tools; simple bold iconography, not tiny text. The cats' paws must touch the keyboard, drawing surface or emerging work.
3. ASSEMBLY AND REVIEW: The Chief of Staff visibly gathers the software, campaign and research sheets into ONE substantial ivory deliverable folder bearing a green approval check and the exact large title "FINISHED WORK". Make this deliverable look finished and valuable. It is handed onward toward Front Desk, not left in a disconnected tray.
4. WORK DELIVERY: At the open far-right workplace boundary, Front Desk hands that same deliverable folder directly to the external teal-coated customer. Front Desk grips the folder's LEFT EDGE while the customer's LEFT PAW grips its RIGHT EDGE. BOTH touch the same folder at the same time. The finished-work exchange must be prominent and unobstructed.
5. PAYMENT IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION: Simultaneously, the customer's RIGHT PAW extends ONE large generic green banknote with a bold "$" to the Treasurer. The Treasurer's paw grips the opposite edge of that SAME banknote. Both visibly touch the payment. Keep this cash exchange BELOW and separate from the work-folder exchange so the two directions are unmistakable. The customer receives work and pays money; they do not receive money. The Treasurer has a small payment terminal or ledger behind this exchange.
6. BOSS GUIDANCE: The grumpy boss watches from behind the central workbench and points at the work being assembled. His gesture ties to the employees' actions. Keep him big enough to recognize, but less dominant than the production and customer exchange.

All four critical visual actions must be easy to see: token insertion, employees making work, customer taking the work, customer handing over payment. Use shared-object paw contact, clear eye-lines and open space. Do not try to explain missing actions with arrows alone. No detached tokens-to-money machine bypassing the employees. No magical money creation.

ROLE AND CUSTOMER LABELS
Place clear cream nameplates or modest scene-anchored captions next to the matching characters, readable at small size:
"Builder", "Grower", "Chief of Staff", "Front Desk", "Researcher", "Treasurer", "Boss", "Customer".
Use exactly one of each. The customer label belongs outside the company boundary. The workbench can also carry the simple stage labels "TOKENS" at the input dock and "PAYMENT" beside the Treasurer's transaction point. The delivered folder itself reads "FINISHED WORK". Do not recreate a freestanding strip of disconnected process trays. Do not add explanatory paragraphs.

BRAND COPY
Keep these exact strings once each, clearly separated from the action:
"OpenCompany"
"AI employees, running on your computer."
"Open source. Your tools. Your control."
Large elegant Newsreader-like serif for the brand, simple readable sans-serif for the rest. Brand area may be compacted to give the full work-and-customer story room, but retain strong hierarchy and generous outside margins. No cropped text or faces.

FORMAT AND QUALITY
One coherent wide landscape banner, approximately 2.3:1. Request a small 1024 x 448 test generation, opaque background. Render for readability at 1024 pixels wide. Slightly enlarge the token tile, delivered folder and green dollar note so their paw contact is clear at draft size. All cats have feline faces, forepaws, ears, tails and tasteful professional attire. No human hands, duplicated arms, extra employees, merged characters, third-party logos, watermarks, earnings amounts, cluttered loose cash, neon or galaxy effects. Use a slightly elevated three-quarter view with enough depth of field for all actions. Prioritize storytelling and understandable physical interaction above decorative architectural detail.

SPECIFIC COMPOSITION
Use the sunlit skylight courtyard, but open up the foreground into one oval central production table. Researcher visibly inserts the cyan token at the rear-left end; Builder and Grower actively make the deliverable at the left/center tools; Chief of Staff assembles the folder at the center-right; Front Desk and Treasurer occupy two neighboring service positions at the open front-right entrance. The visiting teal-coated customer stands on the near side of the counter, external to the employee area. Make the report exchange and reverse-direction cash exchange the large foreground focal point. Boss watches from a small rear balcony, pointing down toward the assembled work. Keep an open clear courtyard center, wide light-oak surfaces, warm ivory plaster, terracotta accents, glass roof and a fully recognizable laptop below.

refinements.name: Courtyard Production and Sale - professional persona polish
refinements.prompt:
Make a precise CHARACTER-PERSONA POLISH of this selected OpenCompany banner. Edit the six employee cats so their expressions, professional tailoring, gaze and small role-specific details clearly match their jobs. This is a refinement of the existing selected artwork, not a new composition.

LOCK THE SELECTED DESIGN
Preserve the camera, architecture, glass skylight, laptop silhouette, warm light, colors, object scale, overall layout, locations of all characters, and readable text. Preserve all eight characters and their identities: six employees, the grumpy Persian boss and the separate customer. Leave the boss and customer visually unchanged. Keep the distinctive coat patterns of all six employees. Their professional clothing should become more intentional and better fitted without changing each role's established color identity.

LOCK THE CRITICAL STORY AND CONTACTS
- Researcher's paw continues to hold the cyan token visibly halfway inside the TOKENS dock.
- The transparent connection from token input to the employee tools remains clear.
- Builder and Grower continue to operate the existing active software/content tools and produce visible work.
- The finished folder remains jointly held between Front Desk and Customer.
- The same green dollar note remains jointly held between Customer and Treasurer, below the folder exchange.
- The customer receives the work and pays the company; never reverse the transaction.
- Boss continues pointing toward the work. Do not add money piles or remove the payment interaction.
Do not break, hide, merge or shift these shared-object paw contacts.

REFINE EACH EMPLOYEE AS A DISTINCT MATURE PROFESSIONAL

1. BUILDER — focused senior software craftsperson.
Keep the ginger tabby and slate-blue overshirt, but make the shirt fit neatly, with crisp rolled cuffs over a simple dark undershirt. Give the cat a concentrated closed-mouth expression, subtly engaged brows and ears angled toward the code screen. Show quiet confidence and technical absorption rather than anger. Slightly purposeful forward lean, paws precisely engaged with the existing keyboard. Preserve the IDE, code deliverable and role label. No construction helmet, tools unrelated to software, extra gadgets or exaggerated nerd costume.

2. GROWER — confident creative growth strategist.
Keep the white cat with its charcoal ear patch, sage blazer and terracotta shirt. Improve blazer tailoring and give the face bright attentive eyes, raised ears and a small assured smile instead of a wide generic cartoon grin. The gaze follows the campaign material on the existing screen. The stylus gesture should look deliberate and imaginative, actively refining content. Upright energetic posture, poised rather than frantic. Preserve the current campaign tools and station. No new props.

3. CHIEF OF STAFF — composed operations coordinator.
Keep the tuxedo coat, navy waistcoat, cream shirt and restrained tie. Give this cat an upright, balanced posture and a calm, observant expression, looking toward the team's in-progress deliverables rather than staring upward. Replace the plain wooden box currently held by this cat with ONE slim, elegant project folio in the same position and at the same approximate scale. Preserve the existing paw grips. The folio is slightly open with three visible index tabs, a simple calendar grid and a short checklist made of abstract marks, no tiny readable writing. This should instantly read as organized priorities, schedules and briefings. Do not add another computer or expand the workstation.

4. FRONT DESK — warm, attentive client-service professional.
Keep the cream colorpoint cat, sable ears, burgundy jacket and discreet headset. Refine the jacket into a tidy well-fitted service blazer. Give the cat warm direct eye contact with the customer, relaxed ears and a reassuring professional smile, not an exaggerated open-mouth reaction. The posture is welcoming and the existing folder handoff is confident and careful. Preserve both characters' grips on the FINISHED WORK folder exactly in the same locations. Keep the headset believable and understated.

5. RESEARCHER — thoughtful evidence-led analyst.
Keep the calico markings, oatmeal cardigan and thin round spectacles. Refine the face with a small thoughtful head tilt, attentive eyes and a quietly inquisitive expression while inspecting the token-fed work process. Neaten the cardigan cuffs and keep the paws recognizably feline. Preserve the visible token insertion grip. Add only one slim open source-comparison notebook tucked flat beside the existing input dock, showing two simple columns of abstract notes; it must not cover the token tiles, TOKENS label, input slot or paw contact. The notebook is a restrained job cue, not a large new feature. No other added objects.

6. TREASURER — precise, trustworthy payment-operations specialist.
Keep the silver tabby markings, forest-green waistcoat, pale shirt and understated reading glasses. Improve the tailoring and give this cat a calm exacting expression, with gaze directed at the incoming payment and terminal. Closed-mouth composure and deliberate posture rather than a grin or excitement about cash. Preserve the extended paw gripping the same dollar note the customer holds, and the other paw's existing working position. Keep the payment terminal and PAYMENT label. Do not turn this role into a trader or depict speculative charts.

COHESIVE CHARACTER CRAFT
All six cats have distinct mature professional personas expressed through feline eyes, ears, muzzles, posture and tailoring. Retain natural feline paws, fur and tails. Improve subtle fur grooming, cloth seams and contact shadows where helpful, but avoid over-detailing or changing the warm handmade miniature aesthetic. No identical facial expressions, baby-cat proportions, human hands, extra limbs, exaggerated costumes or additional characters.

TEXT — PRESERVE EVERY EXISTING STRING, SPELLING AND PLACEMENT
"OpenCompany"
"AI employees, running on your computer."
"Open source. Your tools. Your control."
"Researcher"
"Builder"
"Grower"
"Chief of Staff"
"Front Desk"
"Treasurer"
"Boss"
"Customer"
"TOKENS"
"FINISHED WORK"
"PAYMENT"
Do not duplicate labels, add personality adjectives, change the brand typography or add any new readable text.

OUTPUT
Return one polished edit at the original wide landscape proportions with opaque background. Continue the lightweight draft workflow: request approximately 1024 pixels wide, prioritize legibility at 1024px. This is one carefully refined selected banner, not a grid of variants.
